# toad <a href="https://tractoverse.github.io/toad/"><img src="man/figures/logo.png" align="right" height="138" alt="toad website" /></a>

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/tractoverse/toad/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/tractoverse/toad/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![Codecov test coverage](https://codecov.io/gh/tractoverse/toad/graph/badge.svg)](https://app.codecov.io/gh/tractoverse/toad)
[![pkgdown](https://github.com/tractoverse/toad/actions/workflows/pkgdown.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/tractoverse/toad/actions/workflows/pkgdown.yaml)
[![CRAN status](https://www.r-pkg.org/badges/version/toad)](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=toad)
<!-- badges: end -->

[**toad**](https://tractoverse.github.io/toad/) (Tractography Open Atlas Data)
provides easy access to reference white matter tractography atlases of the
human brain, for benchmarking and anomaly-detection studies of brain
microstructure. It is the data layer of the
[{tractoverse}](https://github.com/tractoverse/tractoverse) package family:
imported bundles are returned as the `streamline`, `bundle`, and `bundle_set`
S7 classes of the [{fiber}](https://tractoverse.github.io/fiber/) package.

Data are hosted as GitHub releases in the package repository and downloaded on
demand — no bulky data files are bundled with the package itself.

## Installation

You can install the development version of toad from
[GitHub](https://github.com/) with:

``` r
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("tractoverse/toad")
```

## Datasets

Two datasets are available (`available_datasets()`):

| Dataset | Bundles | License |
|---|---|---|
| `HCP1065` | 87 population-averaged white matter bundles | [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/) |
| `TractSeg` | 72 tracts segmented in each of 105 HCP subjects | [CC BY-NC 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc/4.0/) — non-commercial |

Both datasets originate from the Human Connectome Project Young Adult dataset;
users must comply with the
[HCP data-use terms](https://www.humanconnectome.org/study/hcp-young-adult/document/wu-minn-hcp-consortium-open-access-data-use-terms).

### HCP1065 population-averaged atlas

A whole-brain tractography atlas averaged across 1,065 healthy adults,
containing 87 white matter bundles each represented as a single
population-level streamline set. Please cite the original work when using it:

> Yeh FC. Population-based tract-to-region connectome of the human brain and
> its hierarchical topology. *Nat Commun* **13**, 4933 (2022).
> <https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-022-32595-4>

```r
# List all available bundles
available_bundles("HCP1065")

# Load one bundle by name
cst_left <- import_bundle("HCP1065", "Left Corticospinal Tract")
# Or use the convenience accessor
cst_left <- HCP1065_CST_L()
```

### TractSeg per-subject bundles

72 white matter tracts segmented in each of 105 HCP Young Adult subjects using
[TractSeg](https://github.com/MIC-DKFZ/TractSeg), redistributed from the
[Zenodo archive](https://zenodo.org/records/1477956)
(DOI: [10.5281/zenodo.1477956](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.1477956)).
Because the segmentation is per-subject, this dataset supports
population-style analyses. Please cite the original TractSeg publication:

> Wasserthal J, Neher P, Maier-Hein KH. TractSeg — Fast and accurate white
> matter tract segmentation. *NeuroImage* **183**, 239–253 (2018).
> <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neuroimage.2018.07.070>

```r
# List all available TractSeg bundles
available_bundles("TractSeg")

# A single subject — returns a bundle
af_left <- import_bundle("TractSeg", "Left Arcuate Fasciculus", subjects = "599469")

# A random sample of 10 subjects — returns a bundle_set
af_sample <- import_bundle("TractSeg", "Left Arcuate Fasciculus", subjects = 10L)
```

## Bundle objects

All bundles are returned as `fiber::bundle` objects:

- `@streamlines` — a list of `streamline` objects, each carrying:
  - `@points` — a $P \times 3$ matrix of 3D coordinates for the $P$ points along the streamline;
  - `@point_data` — a list of per-point attributes (e.g. FA, MD);
  - `@streamline_data` — a list of per-streamline scalars.
- `@bundle_data` — bundle-level metadata (name, source dataset, etc.).

Multi-subject imports return a `fiber::bundle_set`. See the
[getting started](https://tractoverse.github.io/toad/articles/toad.html)
vignette for details, and the
[{fiber}](https://tractoverse.github.io/fiber/) package for working with these
objects.
